instantiated_cells.justification: The statute imposes periodic spending disclosure by requiring registered principals (not lobbyists) to file expense statements on or before July 31 and January 31, and it does not require lobbyists to file an annual spending report.
Expense statements are filed semiannually by principals and lobbyists only supply information to principals, so no monthly lobbyist spending report is required.
The statute assigns the spending report filing obligation to principals (with lobbyists providing information), so there is no 'other' lobbyist-filed periodic spending report cadence.
The only periodic spending statement in the provided text is the principal’s semiannual expense statement, not a quarterly lobbyist spending report.
Semiannual spending reports are required from registered principals, not from lobbyists as named filers of separate spending reports.
The statute requires semiannual filings by principals (Jan. 31 and July 31) and contains no triannual, session-linked lobbyist spending report requirement.

Itemization requirements in §13.68 apply to the principal’s expense statement, while lobbyists merely provide supporting information to the principal rather than file a separate itemized spending report.
The statute requires expense statements from principals and only requires lobbyists to supply information for the principal’s filing, so lobbyists have no separate spending-report filing cadence.
Disclosure of legislative proposals/topics is required of principals as a condition of lobbying, not of lobbyists as separate spend-report filers.

Compensation to lobbyists is included in the principal’s reported lobbying expenditures, but the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to disclose how much they receive from clients in a separate spending report.
The reporting requirement is for principals to disclose time spent meeting with officials and related activities, not for lobbyists to disclose contacts in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Issue-level time proportions are reported by principals in their expense statement, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
The statute requires principals to report each legislative proposal/budget bill subject/rule number or topic, and does not impose a lobbyist-specific issue disclosure in a separate spending report.
Activity disclosures about proposals/topics are a principal reporting obligation under §13.67(1), not a lobbyist-filed spending report requirement.

The principal’s expense statement includes various categories of lobbying expenditures, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate report disclosing gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging.
Indirect lobbying costs are disclosed in the principal’s expense statement, and lobbyists are not required to file their own separate spending report disclosing such costs.

Because lobbyists are not required to file separate itemized spending reports (they only provide information to principals), the statute does not mandate the described lobbyist itemized report with issues/bill numbers and compensation.
The periodic expense statement required by §13.68 is filed by principals, and there is no lobbyist-filed spending report requiring disclosure of the lobbyist’s address and phone number.

The statute’s requirement to report legislative proposals/topics is imposed on principals, so lobbyists do not have a separate reporting duty to reveal bills/actions (with or without position) in a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Business-activity/nature information is required in the principal’s registration statement, not as a disclosure by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
Lobbyist authorizations are filed with the commission but the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed spending report disclosing principals’ address and phone number.

A lobbyist license entitles practice on behalf of each registered principal with filed authorizations, but there is no requirement that lobbyists file a separate spending report listing all principals represented.
Bill/rule number and topic reporting is imposed on principals under §13.67(1), not on lobbyists in a separate lobbyist spending report.
Direct lobbying costs such as compensation to lobbyists are reported by principals as part of their expense statement, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.

Total lobbying expenditures are reported as an aggregate total in the principal’s expense statement, and the statute does not require lobbyists to report total expenditures in their own separate spending report.
No lobbyist-filed itemized spending report is required (only principal expense statements with lobbyist-supplied information), so the described lobbyist-report regime does not exist.
The statute’s periodic reporting obligation applies to principals filing expense statements and does not impose a lobbyist 'no activity' report requirement.

The statute provides an exception for furnishing things of value to a lobbyist’s relative/household member and does not require lobbyists to file a spending report, so there is no lobbyist spending-report requirement to report spending on household members of public officials.
Although principals must provide certain itemized information in their expense statement, lobbyists are not required to disclose spending in an itemized format in a separate lobbyist-filed report.
